close_reason: Fixed in commit 08b1919 alongside .70. Added 'Diagnostic content convention' section to apply_space_metadata_patch rustdoc and an equivalent paragraph in apply_space_patch's per-op error semantics table. SetError.description MUST contain the missing-permission identifier as a substring; 'SetError::new(Forbidden).with_description("manage_space permission required")' is the canonical form. Replaced misleading 'SetError::new(Forbidden)' literal in the metadata-patch return-value section that would have a backend fail the kit's own tests.
description:
## Finding

Four integration tests across three test files assert that the
`SetError.description` field on permission-denied / hierarchy-
violation / last-admin-protection rejections CONTAINS specific
permission identifier substrings:

```
crate-jmap-chat-server/tests/space_metadata_apply.rs:298-304
    assert!(desc.contains("manage_space"), ...)

crate-jmap-chat-server/tests/channel_category_apply.rs:196-202
    assert!(desc.contains("manage_channels"), ...)

crate-jmap-chat-server/tests/role_member_apply.rs:294-300
    assert!(desc.contains("hierarchy") || desc.contains("position"), ...)

crate-jmap-chat-server/tests/role_member_apply.rs:574-580
    assert!(desc.contains("last-admin") || desc.contains("manage_members"), ...)
```

Yet the rustdoc for both backend methods is silent on the
`description` content convention:

**`apply_space_patch`** (`backend.rs:497-502`) — discusses per-op
rejection routing into `OpResult.outcome` but says nothing about
the description string content.

**`apply_space_metadata_patch`** (`backend.rs:563-564`):

```
/// `Err(BackendSetError::SetError(SetError::new(Forbidden)))`
/// when the caller fails the `manage_space` gate.
```

`SetError::new(Forbidden)` constructs a SetError with an empty
description by default — but the test at
`space_metadata_apply.rs:298-304` asserts the description names
the permission. The rustdoc literally suggests the wrong builder
call: a backend that follows the doc verbatim writes a
description-less SetError and fails the kit's own test.

## What goes wrong for a third-party implementer

A backend that returns the rustdoc-prescribed
`SetError::new(Forbidden)` (or `SetError::with_type(Forbidden)`)
with no `description`:

1. Passes the rustdoc contract (Forbidden is the correct variant)
2. Fails the kit's integration test suite when plugged in
3. Breaks downstream UI/CLI consumers that surface the
   description to end users — the user sees "Permission denied"
   instead of "Permission denied: missing manage_space" and
   cannot diagnose what to ask an admin for.
4. Breaks consumers that programmatically extract permission
   identifiers from descriptions to drive permission-request
   flows.

## Recommendation

Add a "Diagnostic content convention" sub-section to both
backend methods. Wording suggestion:

> ## Diagnostic content convention
>
> When the rejection is permission-denied, backends SHOULD set
> `SetError.description` to a string containing the missing
> permission identifier as a substring (`"manage_space"`,
> `"manage_channels"`, `"manage_members"`, `"manage_roles"`, or
> a deployment-specific permission name). Consumers may rely on
> the description substring to route permission-request flows.
> The kit's integration tests assert this substring match; a
> backend that returns a bare `SetError::new(Forbidden)` with
> empty description will fail those tests.
>
> Similarly, hierarchy-violation rejections SHOULD include
> `"hierarchy"` or `"position"`, last-admin-protection
> rejections SHOULD include `"last-admin"` or
> `"manage_members"`.

Alternative: use `SetError::with_extra` (or analogous) to put a
structured `missingPermission` extra field on the error instead
of relying on substring matching. This is more robust against
locale-variation in the description but requires consumer-side
opt-in.

## Engineering basis

- 4 test assertions read verbatim, all asserting `contains()` on
  the description string.
- Rustdoc passages on both backend methods read verbatim.
- The kit's reference `MemoryBackend` includes the permission
  identifier in its SetError descriptions (e.g. at
  `memory.rs:2686-2696` for `permissions::required_permissions_for_op`
  output) — implementation matches the test but the doc does not.

## Scope note

This is one of several "tests encode contract that rustdoc does
not" gaps surfaced by the 4th-pass test-as-implicit-contract
exercise. Combined with the per-op SetError variant table gap
(separate finding), the single highest-leverage fix is one new
"Per-op error semantics" sub-section on `apply_space_patch`
covering both the SetErrorType variant table and the
description content convention. Same pattern applies to
`apply_space_metadata_patch`.
title: API contract: apply_space_patch / apply_space_metadata_patch rustdoc is silent on the diagnostic 'description' content convention; tests assert description names the missing permission
